text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I ran a broad kernel 'stripe' sweep to compare Flash variants, paged-attn, and fused kernels under our real batching mix. Wanted to surface findings before I open a formal PR.

miriam: Nice. What workload and pools?

alex: prod-like traces (mix of short chat + embed tails), model=redwood-8k, seq distribution ~ [16, 64, 512], batcher config: dynamic target=64, max=128. ran on ded-gpu-pool-3 (A100-80GB equivalents).

li: high level numbers? tokens/sec and cost/M?

alex: Quick summary table from the profiler (median across 10 runs):
```
kernel_variant | kv_hit_rate | tokens/s | $/M_tokens_est
--------------------------------------------------
flash_v2       | 0.78        | 5,600    | 1.65
paged_attn     | 0.92        | 4,700    | 1.95
fused_attn     | 0.62        | 6,100    | 1.58
flash_v1       | 0.80        | 5,100    | 1.81
```
Notes: $/M estimate uses our current token cost model (GPU runtime + infra overhead).

sam: Interesting that fused is fastest but lower kv_hit. Any idea why fused loses KV locality?

alex: Hypothesis: fused's memory layout favours compute throughput but evicts KV cache earlier because of larger working set when batching; observed higher cross-layer mem copy count in perf counters.

jt: Can you paste the perf counter snippet?

alex: Sure — here's a small excerpt from nvprof-style dump showing memcpy counts and L2 reads (normalized):
```
variant: fused_attn
L2_reads: 1.00
memcpy_calls: 23
kv_cache_evictions: 0.18

variant: flash_v2
L2_reads: 0.78
memcpy_calls: 14
kv_cache_evictions: 0.09
```

miriam: So fused wins raw tokens/s but costs less on $/M because runtime is better despite kv churn? The table shows fused slightly cheaper than flash_v2. Why is paged_attn more expensive?

alex: Paged has higher kv_hit_rate in the traces but its kernel is heavier per token (more page handling overhead). In our run the extra control flow and page management reduced overall tokens/s and raised $/M. Paged gives better tail latencies and steadier perf though.

li: Any regressions vs last week's baseline?

alex: Compared to last week's autoscaler-batching tweak baseline (same batcher), flash_v2 improved tokens/s by ~9%, fused improved by ~18%, paged dropped ~6%. But we saw a regression in fused for long-seq (>1024) cases: latency percentile jumped ~2x in those tails.

sam: That's worrying for large-context workloads. Where does the latency spike come from?

alex: Traced it to a fallback path when KV beyond a threshold triggers a tiled-swap. The fused kernel currently lacks a graceful partial-kv path, so it stalls and forces synchronous swap.

jt: Can we mitigate in the short term by changing batching heuristics? e.g., favor smaller batches for long-seq requests or prioritize kv-hot requests?

alex: I ran a small experiment: bias batcher to prefer requests with kv_hit_est > 0.6 and cap dynamic batch to 48 for seq>1024. Result: fused long-seq p99 dropped back to acceptable levels, tokens/s overall down by ~4% but $/M for long-seq improved a lot.

miriam: Sounds like a plausible interim. Do we have CI benchmarks reproducible?

alex: CI-bot produced artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/stripe-sweep/1719412345 (perf logs + flamegraphs). Also attached a small driver we used:
```bash
# driver snippet
python bench_driver.py --model redwood-8k --trace sample_traces/2025-11-mix.json \
  --batcher dynamic --target 64 --max-batch 128 --variants flash_v2,paged_attn,fused_attn,flash_v1
```

ci-bot: Benchmark run completed. Artifacts archived at the URL alex pasted.

li: For the $/M calc — are we including prefix cache savings (KV hits reduce compute)?

alex: Yes the estimator subtracts estimated token compute when kv_hit true. But we should be careful: fused's higher raw throughput reduces amortized overhead, so $/M has two competing effects.

sam: Proposed next steps: 1) open small runtime PR to add partial-kv path in fused; 2) add batcher rule to prefer kv-hot requests and cap batch size for very long seq; 3) run nightly sweep with tails emphasized.

miriam: Agreed. Alex can you draft the PR with the perf numbers and include short mitigations? Add a changelog entry for the batcher tweak.

alex: Will do, I'll bundle the driver + flamegraphs + the p99/median tables. Expect PR tomorrow.

jt: One last ask — can we output per-layer kv eviction traces per run? That would help the kernel authors.

alex: Good call — I'll add per-layer eviction counters to the bench harness and re-run overnight.

miriam: Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: :eyes:
